Mullet
MUL-it
noun (Gen X slang)
The haircut — short on the top and sides, long in the back — was everywhere in the 1980s and early 1990s, from hockey rinks to country music (Billy Ray Cyrus, "Achy Breaky Heart," 1992) to prime-time television. It had no settled name until the Beastie Boys named it in their song "Mullet Head" (1994), drawing on the old American insult mullethead, a dull, thick-headed fellow. The catchphrase "business in the front, party in the back" followed later in the 1990s. The older English mullet is the fish.

Definition · Webster 1828 · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

Biblical Definition

The mullet is the haircut Gen X would rather forget and cannot: short in front, long in back, "business in the front, party in the back." It crowned hockey players, country singers, and half the yearbook in 1987. The name came late, after its heyday, from a 1994 Beastie Boys song and an old insult for a dull fellow — a sign the culture had already begun laughing at it. The Christian observation is gentle: hairstyles come and go, and the Bible is not a style guide. "The very hairs of your head are all numbered" (Mat 10:30); God cares about the man under the hair far more than its cut. Still, Scripture has one famous haircut story, and it is a warning. Absalom was the most praised man in Israel "for his beauty: from the sole of his foot even to the crown of his head there was no blemish in him" (2Sa 14:25), and he weighed his yearly trimmings like treasure. In the end, riding in rebellion against his father, "his head caught hold of the oak" (2Sa 18:9), and the glory he was proud of held him fast for his enemies. Pride in appearance is a slow trap. Peter points to a better adornment than any style: "the hidden man of the heart" and "the ornament of a meek and quiet spirit" (1Pe 3:4). The only hairstyle Proverbs praises is gray: "The hoary head is a crown of glory, if it be found in the way of righteousness" (Pro 16:31). A father can pull out the old photos and laugh with his kids. Then he can tell them: the cut will date you; the heart is what God sees.

Webster 1828 Definition

The 1980s haircut, short in front and long in back, named after its heyday by the Beastie Boys’ "Mullet Head" (1994); a harmless fashion with a quiet warning from Absalom, whose proud head caught hold of the oak (2Sa 18:9).

MULLET, n. (Gen X slang, named 1994; the style itself 1980s–early 1990s) A haircut cropped short on the top and sides and left long at the back. "Look at Uncle Rick’s mullet in the 1988 family photo."

Named by the Beastie Boys’ "Mullet Head" (1994), from the American insult mullethead, a dull fellow; catchphrase "business in the front, party in the back."

Associated with hockey, country music (Billy Ray Cyrus, 1992), and 1980s television; revived ironically in the 2010s–20s.

Webster 1828: MULLET, n. [Latin mullus.] A fish of the genus Mugil. The lips are membranaceous; the inferior one carinated inwards; it has no teeth, and the body is of a whitish color. This fish frequents the shore and roots in the sand like a hog. It is an excellent fish for the table.

Decode for parents: laugh at the old photos together; teach that God numbers the hairs and looks on the heart.

Key Scripture

Mat 10:30 — "But the very hairs of your head are all numbered."

2Sa 14:25 — "But in all Israel there was none to be so much praised as Absalom for his beauty: from the sole of his foot even to the crown of his head there was no blemish in him."

2Sa 18:9 — "And Absalom met the servants of David. And Absalom rode upon a mule, and the mule went under the thick boughs of a great oak, and his head caught hold of the oak, and he was taken up between the heaven and the earth; and the mule that was under him went away."

1Pe 3:4 — "But let it be the hidden man of the heart, in that which is not corruptible, even the ornament of a meek and quiet spirit, which is in the sight of God of great price."

Pro 16:31 — "The hoary head is a crown of glory, if it be found in the way of righteousness."

Modern Corruption

The mullet is a harmless fashion now worn mostly as a joke; Scripture neither condemns nor commends a haircut, but warns through Absalom that pride in one’s looks is a trap.

expand to see more

Fashion and its expiration date. The mullet is the clearest proof that appearance is a moving target: the cut that looked sharp in 1987 looked ridiculous by 1997, and its very name was an insult. Children who page through the old yearbooks learn a useful lesson early: the world’s idea of good-looking changes every decade, so it is a poor foundation for a life. "man looketh on the outward appearance, but the LORD looketh on the heart" (1Sa 16:7). A haircut can be laughed at; a heart has to be tended.

Absalom’s hair. Scripture’s one great haircut story is about pride. Absalom was praised from sole to crown (2Sa 14:25) and weighed his trimmings each year, and the glory he cultivated caught in an oak and held him for the spears (2Sa 18:9). The point is not that long hair is wicked; it is that what a man is proud of can become what holds him. Peter’s adornment — the meek and quiet spirit, of great price in God’s sight (1Pe 3:4) — never goes out of style.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Latin mullus → English mullet (the fish) → American mullethead (a dullard) → Beastie Boys’ "Mullet Head" (1994) names the 1980s haircut; Scripture: the LORD looketh on the heart (1Sa 16:7).

19th-c. American mullethead — a dull, thick-headed person

1980s–early 1990s: the short-front, long-back haircut, unnamed at its peak

1994: the Beastie Boys’ "Mullet Head" gives the style its name

Biblical hair: numbered by God (Mat 10:30); Absalom’s pride caught in the oak (2Sa 18:9)
